questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Buddhist architectural marvel of India?
questions.solution:
• Not Buddhist Marvel: Pataleshwar Caves
  • Fact: Pataleshwar (Pune) is an 8th-century rock-cut Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva. Sanchi, Bharhut, and Ajanta are all Buddhist.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first President (temporary) of the Constituent Assembly of India, when it met on 9 December 1946?
questions.solution:
• First Temporary President: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
  • Assembly: He presided over the first meeting on 9 December 1946; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President two days later.

questions.question: he popular style of temple architecture in northern India is called ________.
questions.solution:
• Northern Temple Style: Nagara
  • Architecture: While Nagara is the North Indian style, Dravida is the South Indian style. Shikara refers to the mountain-like spire of the temple.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for slowing down of the Non-cooperation Movement?
questions.option_1: Many lawyers resigned but then absence of income for a longer period of time compelled them to rejoin.
questions.option_2: Due to the absence of alternative Indian institution, boycott of British institutions posed a problem.
questions.option_3: Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
questions.option_4: Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth and poor people could not afford to buy it.
questions.solution:
• Non-Cooperation Slowdown: Leaders shifting to domestic work (Incorrect Reason)
  • Actual Reasons: High cost of Khadi, lack of alternative Indian institutions (schools/courts), and financial pressure on lawyers.

questions.question: In which year did the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II appoint the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Diwani Rights (1765): 1765
  • Event: Following the Battle of Buxar, Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the right to collect revenues of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.

questions.question: Ashoka fought a war to conquer Kalinga. Kalinga was the ancient name of coastal ______.
questions.solution:
• Kalinga Location: Orissa (Odisha)
  • History: Kalinga was the ancient name for coastal Odisha, where Ashoka fought his final, life-changing war.

questions.question: Which famous Rashtrakuta king built the rock-cut temple of Kailash at Ellora?
questions.solution:
• Kailash Temple (Ellora): King Krishna I
  • Note: This massive monolithic structure was carved out of a single rock from the top down during the Rashtrakuta reign.

questions.question: ho among the following Gupta rulers is known as the 'Napoleon of India’?
questions.solution:
• Napoleon of India: Samudragupta
  • Origin: Historian V.A. Smith called him this due to his extensive military conquests and undefeated record.

questions.question: ho among the following was the first Indian to be selected to the British ‘House of Commons’ on a Liberal Party ticket?
questions.solution:
• Grand Old Man of India: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Fact: He was the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons (1892) and founded the 'Drain of Wealth' theory.

questions.question: ______ was the capital of the Pandya dynasty.
questions.solution:
• Pandya Capital: Madurai
  • Detail: Madurai was the seat of the Pandyas and a major center for the Tamil Sangam literature.

questions.question: Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur is one of the largest temples in India and is an example of Dravidian architecture during the ______ period.
questions.solution:
• Brihadeshwara Temple: Chola
  • Builder: Built by Rajaraja I at Thanjavur, it is a hallmark of Dravidian architecture.

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the Champaran movement against the indigo planters?
questions.solution:
• Champaran Satyagraha: 1917
  • Significance: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India, fought for the rights of indigo farmers under the 'Tinkathia' system.

questions.question: ho founded Shantiniketan near Bolpur on 22 December 1901?
questions.solution:
• Shantiniketan Founder: Rabindranath Tagore
  • Note: It started as a small school in 1901 and later evolved into the Visva-Bharati University.

questions.question: y maternal descent, Mughals were descendants of ?
questions.solution:
• Mughal Descent (Maternal): Genghis Khan
  • Lineage: From their father's side, they were descendants of Timur; from their mother's side, they were descendants of the Mongol ruler Genghis Khan.

questions.question: Zoroaster was a/an ______ prophet.
questions.solution:
• Zoroaster: Iranian
  • Religion: He was an ancient Iranian prophet who founded Zoroastrianism (the religion of the Parsis).

questions.question: Who set up the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Asiatic Society of Bengal: William Jones
  • 1784: Founded to encourage Oriental research and translate Indian texts into English.

questions.question: ho among the following founded Arya Samaj in 1875?
questions.solution:
• Arya Samaj Founder: Swami Dayanand Saraswati
  • Goal: Founded in 1875 in Bombay with the slogan "Back to the Vedas."

questions.question: utbuddin Aybak ruled over Delhi from ______.
questions.solution:
• Qutubuddin Aibak: 1206 to 1210
  • History: The founder of the Slave Dynasty; he died in 1210 after falling from a horse while playing Chaugan (Polo).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct?
I. Gautama Buddha belonged to a small gana known as the Sakya gana and was a Kshatriya.
II. Gautama Buddha passed away at Kusinara.
questions.solution:
• Buddha's Life: Both I and II
  • Facts: He belonged to the Sakya Gana (Kshatriya) and attained Mahaparinirvana (death) at Kusinara (Kushinagar).

questions.question: Richard Wellesley was the Governor - General of India from ______.
questions.solution:
• Lord Wellesley: 1798 – 1805
  • Policy: Famous for introducing the 'Subsidiary Alliance' to expand British influence over Indian states.

questions.question: ho among the following led of the famous Indigo Revolt in Bengal?
questions.option_2: Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas
questions.solution:
• Indigo Revolt (1859): Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas
  • Note: Started in Nadia, Bengal, against the forced cultivation of indigo; famously portrayed in the play 'Nil Darpan'.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers did NOT belong to Maurya dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Not a Maurya: Bimbisara
  • Correction: Bimbisara was the founder of the Haryanka Dynasty. Bindusara (Ashoka's father) was the Maurya ruler.

questions.question: Genghis Khan died in which year?
questions.solution:
• Death of Genghis Khan: 1227
  • Legacy: His empire was divided among his sons, but his Mongol invasion patterns influenced the Delhi Sultanate's policies later on.
